items.title: Ich geh und suche mit Verlangen, BWV 49
items.description: Johann Sebastian Bach composed the church cantata Ich geh und suche mit Verlangen, BWV 49, in Leipzig for the twentieth Sunday after Trinity Sunday and first performed it on 3 November 1726. It is a solo cantata, a dialogue for soprano and bass.

items.title: Haley Stevens
items.description: Haley Maria Stevens is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative from Michigan's 11th congressional district since 2019. Elected as a member of the Democratic Party, Stevens represents most of urbanized Oakland County, including many of Detroit's northern suburbs.

items.title: Learjet 60
items.description: The Learjet 60 is a mid-size cabin, medium-range business jet aircraft that was manufactured by Bombardier Aerospace in Wichita, Kansas. Powered by two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW305A engines, it has a range of 2,405 nautical miles (4,454 km) with NBAA 100 nmi (190 km) reserves, ISA. items.title: Susan Saint James
items.description: Susan Saint James was an American actress. In 1968, she landed a role as Peggy Maxwell on the TV series The Name of the Game. Saint James received three Emmy Award nominations for the series, winning once in 1969. items.title: Abdul El-Sayed
items.description: Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed is an American epidemiologist, public health administrator, academic and politician who is the Democratic nominee in the 2026 United States Senate election in Michigan.

items.title: 2026 Palm Beach County Learjet 60 crash
items.description: On November 1, 2026, a privately owned Learjet 60 business jet crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, United States. The flight was traveling from Austin–Bergstrom International Airport in Texas to North Eleuthera Airport in The Bahamas. The plane crashed after a high speed descent, killing all nine people on board and injuring a person on the ground.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli
items.description: Andrea Kimi Antonelli is an Italian racing driver who competes in Formula One for Mercedes. Antonelli won the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2026 with Mercedes, becoming the youngest-ever World Drivers' Champion; he has won nine Grands Prix since his debut in 2025.
